description:
Commit fb5dbaf migrated nine `Option<String>` fields to `Option<UTCDate>` in this crate (Task.created, .updated, .utc_start, .utc_due, .progress_updated; CheckItem.updated; Comment.created, .updated; TaskNotification.created; TaskFilterCondition.after/.before; TaskNotificationFilterCondition.after/.before).

UTCDate is defined in crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs as a `#[serde(transparent)]` newtype over String. `validate_utcdate` is a fallible constructor only invoked by `UTCDate::new_validated`. Deserialization (via #[serde(transparent)]) bypasses validation completely.

Consequence: a server response like `"created": "not-a-date"` or `"updated": "2024-01-19T18:00:00"` (no Z suffix — missing RFC 8620 §1.4 timezone marker) deserializes successfully. The fields gain typed-newtype labeling but zero validation power at the boundary.

This is not a regression — the previous String form was equally permissive — but the migration's claimed benefit (type safety at the wire boundary) is not delivered. The fields look stricter than they are.

Maintenance consequence: contributors will look at `Option<UTCDate>` and assume the deserializer rejects malformed timestamps. They will write downstream code that assumes the inner string is `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` and is surprised when an upstream server's sloppy response slips through.

Fix options:
  (a) Add a custom Deserialize impl on UTCDate that calls validate_utcdate. This is a workspace-level decision — has to be made in jmap-types, propagates to every UTCDate-typed field everywhere. File against jmap-types if pursued.
  (b) Leave as-is but add a rustdoc note to UTCDate explicitly stating "Deserialization does not validate format; use new_validated if you need a checked constructor."

This review files the finding here; the decision belongs to jmap-types maintainership.
title: UTCDate newtype migration provides no deserialize-time validation
